 J U D G M E N T

This petition is filed by the petitioner U/s.166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of .50,00,000/- along with interest from the date of petition till its realization for injuries sustained by him in the accident.

2. The case of the petitioner in brief is that on 20.06.2018 at about 05.45 p.m., while petitioner was crossing the road near his school's back gate, the respondent No.2 drove White Swift Car bearing Regn.No.KA-05-AG-0444, at high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against petitioner.
Due to said accident, petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Thereafter,
petitioner was shifted to CMH Hospital, Indiranagar, Bengaluru and then shifted to St.John's Medical College Hospital, Sarjapur Road, Koramangala, Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and spent a sum of .5,00,000/- towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges.

entities.text: St.John's Medical College Hospital, Sarjapur Road
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Prior to the accident, petitioner was hale and healthy and was aged about 17 years and was working as a Security Guard and also used to Supply milk in the said locality and was earning a sum of .45,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries, petitioner suffered permanent disability.
The accident occurred only due to rash and negligent driving of car by its driver.
The respondents, being the insurer and owner of the offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
3. In spite of service of notice, respondent No.1 appeared before the tribunal through the counsel and filed the written statement.

The respondent No.2 did not appear before the tribunal and hence,
he has been placed ex-parte.
4. In the Written Statement, the respondent No.1 has denied the contents of claim petition specifically and categorically.
Further the respondent No.1 also denied age, occupation and income of petitioner as well as place, time and manner of accident.
Further respondent No.1 contended that the petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable either in law or on facts and same is liable to be dismissed.

Further respondent No.1 contended that swift dzire car was insured with them under the policy No.MOQ1156952 which was valid from 07.03.2010 to 08.08.2018 and the liability, if any,
is subject to the terms and conditions of policy.

Further contended that the petitioner is physically Mahesh vs Royal Sun All Ins Co Ltd on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149864305/
2 impaired (deaf and dumb since birth) and was studying in NRSD School and Hostel,
Jeevanbheemangara, Bengaluru school for special children.

sentences.text: The amount claimed by the petitioner is highly exorbitant.
Hence, prayed for dismissal of petition.

5. On the basis of above pleadings, the learned predecessor in office framed the following:
ISSUES 1.

Whether petitioner proves that, he sustained grievous injuries in the accident that occurred on 20.06.2018 at about 05.45 p.m., near NRSD School and Hostel Back Gate, Jeevanbheemanagar, Bengaluru, while he was crossing the road, due to the rash and negligent driving of LMV Car bearing Regn.No.KA- 05-AG-0444 by its driver?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed in the claim petition?

If so, what is the quantum of compensation and from whom?
3.
What order or award?
6. In order to prove the contentions of the petition, the natural guardian/father of petitioner examined himself as PW.1 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.21 and closed his side of evidence.
The respondents did not adduce their evidence either oral or documentary.

7. Heard the argument of both sides and perused the materials available on record.
8.

The petitioner contended that on 20.06.2018 at about 05.45 p.m., accident occurred near NRSD School and Hostel Back Gate, Jeevanbheemanagar, Bengaluru, while he was crossing the road, due to the rash and negligent driving of LMV Swift Dzire Car bearing Regn.No.KA-05-AG-0444 by its driver in which he sustained grievous injuries.

10. In order to prove rash and negligent driving of LMV Swift Dzire Car bearing Regn.No.KA-05-AG-0444 by its driver, the natural guardian/father of petitioner got examined as Mahesh vs Royal Sun All Ins Co Ltd on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149864305/

sentences.text: In the chief examination, PW.1 deposed that due to rash and negligent driving of car by its driver, the accident occurred.
On perusal of cross-examination of PW.1 nothing has been elicited from the mouth of PW.1 to disprove the case of petitioner.
11. Further, in order to prove accident, the petitioner has produced Ex.P.1 & 2 FIR and first information.
On perusal of Ex.P.2 first information, one person by name Sri.Rajanna.N S/o.Nanjunadaswamy has lodged complaint with police on 21.06.2018 with respect to the accident occurred on 20.06.2018.
On the basis of first information lodged, the police registered the FIR as per Ex.P.1 for the offence punishable U/s.279 & 337 of IPC.
In the first information statement as well as FIR, the accident is stated to have been caused due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by its driver.
The accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
The petitioner also furnished spot mahazar and sketch which are marked as Ex.P.4 and 5.
The said documents disclose that the police visited the place of incident after registration of FIR and the place of incident is described in the said document.

In the mahazar also,
the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
On perusal of sketch, it depicts the aspect of deviation of car from its normal course before causing the accident.
The sketch does not depict the aspect of presence of road in order to consider that the driver of offending car intended to take a turn and changed the course of his way in that regard.
The sketch does not disclose the aspect of existence of road in order to change the course by the driver of offending car.
No explanation is forthcoming related to purpose for which the driver of the car changed the course of the car, as depicted in the sketch.
The said documents indicate the aspect of negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
The respondents not placed any satisfactory materials in order to show that the facts at the place of accident differ from the facts as shown in mahazar and sketch.
Ex.P.6 is the wound certificate which discloses the aspect of injuries sustained by the petitioner.
Ex.P.7 is the IMV Reports, wherein the damages caused to the vehicle are mentioned.
Inspection of the vehicle will be conducted after seizure of the vehicle by police.
The respondent No.2 does not appear to have questioned the aspect of seizure of vehicle by police.
The said document discloses the aspect of involvement of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
Ex . P9 is the notice issued under Sec.133 of IMV Act and reply given to the said notice is marked as Ex.P.10.
In Ex.P.9, notice given by I.O, it is mentioned that the offending car has been involved in the accident and negligence on the part of driver of offending car is the cause for the accident.
The respondent No.2 appears to have given reply to the notice which is marked as Ex.P.10.
In the reply to the notice, respondent No.2 does not appear to have denied the aspect of involvement of the car in the accident.
Further, respondent No.2 also does not appear to have denied negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
Respondent No.2, being the owner of offending vehicle, could have denied the involvement of car in the accident and negligence of driver of car in the cause of accident.
But, respondent No.2 does not appear to have stated said aspects in the reply given to the notice.
The I.O., after completion of investigation, filed the final report against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offence punishable U/s.279 & 338 of IPC as per Ex.P.11.
In the final report also, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
The police filed the final report after detailed investigation.
The driver or owner of offending vehicle does not appear to have questioned the correctness of the investigation.
No satisfactory materials are placed by the respondents to show that the investigation is not conducted in a proper manner.

sentences.text: In the FIR as well as final report, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle which aspect does not appear to have been challenged in any manner.
The respondents not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to rebut or controvert the documents furnished by petitioner related to negligence of driver of offending vehicle.
PW.1 is cross examined on behalf of respondents and in the cross examination also, nothing to disprove or disbelieve the contention of petitioners could be elicited.

No satisfactory materials are being placed before the Tribunal to disprove the contention of petitioners pertaining to the aspect of negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
12. The respondents not placed satisfactory materials before the tribunal to disprove case of petitioner.
In the absence of sufficient and satisfactory materials to the contrary, the documents furnished by the petitioner are to be considered for ascertaining the aspect of negligence.
The respondents not furnished any materials to show that there is no negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
The respondents placed nothing before the tribunal to disprove case of petitioner.
On perusal of entire record, it discloses that the driver of insured vehicle driven the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against petitioner.

Under these circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 coupled with the documents produced as per Exs.P.1 to P.11, this tribunal is of the opinion that the accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Swift Dzire Car bearing Regn.No.KA-05-AG-0444 by its driver and same has resulted in injuries to the Petitioner.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 held in the Affirmative.
13. Issue No.2:
In view of answering issue No.1 in the affirmative, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.

In order to assess the compensation, the Tribunal has to look into several factors like injury, pain and suffering sustained by the petitioner and amount spent by the petitioner towards medical expenses, food and extra nourishment and medical attendants, conveyance, loss of income during the treatment, disability, loss of amenities etc.
14.
The Guardian and next friend of minor petitioner contended that due to accident petitioner sustained injuries.
In order to prove the injuries sustained by petitioner, the Natural Guardian of petitioner has produced wound certificate issued by St.John's Medical College Hospital, Bengaluru marked at Ex.P.6.

On perusal of Ex.P.6, it reveals that the petitioner sustained graze abrasion over the left scapular area, abrasion present over the occipital protuberance, crush injury to the left foot extending from ankle up to the toes measuring 12x8 cms.
The wound certificate reveals that the doctor has opined that injury No.1 & 2 are simple in nature and injury No.3 is grievous in nature.
The petitioner has produced Ex.P.12 - discharge summary issued by St.Johns Medical College and Hospital to show that the petitioner has taken treatment as an inpatient.

The discharge summary discloses that the doctor diagnosed the petitioner and stated that petitioner sustained post traumatic left foot degloving injury and underwent procedure debridement on 21.06.18 under GA,
debridement with free ALT flap + SSG for donor defect (recipient anterior tibial artery with accompanying vene commentantes, donor ALT flap on the descending branch of the lateral circumflex femoral artery) done on 03.07.2018 under GA.
The petitioner has also produced 97 medical bills amounting to .3,24,613/- marked at Ex.P.16.
The respondents not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to rebut or disprove the medical bills furnished by petitioner.

Further,

sentences.text: in order to prove disability, the petitioner neither produced disability certificate nor examined the doctor.
The petitioner has not examined the doctor to prove his disability and the implications of injuries to his future.
As per the materials on record, the petitioner is a student and stated to be studying 9th standard.
The petitioner not furnished any satisfactory materials to show that the accidental injuries hampered his education.
The petitioner not furnished any satisfactory materials to show that his education got hampered due to the accidental injuries.
The petitioner also not examined the doctor in order to show that the injuries caused to the petitioner hampered his education.
So, in the absence of proper evidence, this tribunal cannot award compensation under the head of future loss of income and other heads.

By considering the facts and circumstances of the case and also the injuries sustained by the petitioner, the petitioner is entitled for Global compensation of .5,00,000/-.
15.

In view of ratio and dictum laid down by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA.No.100090 of 2014 C/w. MFA.No.25107 of 2013 between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs.
Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another, the petitioner is entitled for interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.

sentences.text: 16. The petitioner has filed petition against the respondents No.1 & 2.
It is already held that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Swift Dzire Car bearing Regn.No.KA-05-AG- 0444 by its driver.
There appears to be no dispute with respect to the ownership of respondent No.2 pertaining to offending vehicle and issue of policy of insurance by respondent No.1 pertaining to offending vehicle.

The materials on record disclose that the offending vehicle was having valid and effective policy of insurance and the driver of offending vehicle was having valid and effective licence at the time of accident.
So, the respondent No.1 & 2, being the insurer and owner of the offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, Issue No.2 answered Partly in the Affirmative.
17. Issue No.3:

In view of the findings given on the above said issues, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following:
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of MV Act is allowed in part with costs.
The petitioner is entitled to a total compensation of .5,00,000/- (Rupees Five Lakhs only) with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of petition till its realization.
Respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and  severally liable to pay compensation to  petitioner.
Respondent No.1 being the insurer is primarily liable to deposit the said compensation amount within a period of two months from the date of award.
Entire compensation amount shall be released in favour of petitioner as amount is meager one.
